pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: btusb: remove HCI_QUIRK_STRICT_DUPLICATE_FILTER bit This removes the HCI_QUIRK_STRICT_DUPLICATE_FILTER bit from the Intel USB driver block in btusb_probe(). There is a conflict intention on receiving advertising reports in BlueZ where the Filter_Duplicates flag is set so strict filtering with RSSI will be applied to Intel BT controllers. However, BlueZ checks if HCI_QUIRK_STRICT_DUPLICATE_FILTER is set and restarts LE scan if the bit is set in order to obtain the advertising reports dropped due to the strict filtering. By removing the bit, BlueZ will not frequently restart LE scanning. BUG=b:64731753 TEST=emerge-eve sys-kernel/chromeos-kernel-4_4 ./update_kernel.sh --remote <IP to DUT> Make sure /sys/kernel/debug/bluetooth/hci0/quirk_strict_duplicate_filter on DUT is "N". CQ-DEPEND=CL:677741 Change-Id: Id14e4e1ea3a3d0d9eac448f341bb839ebf4d373f Signed-off-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/677740 Reviewed-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com>

CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: set Filter_Duplicates parameter to 0x00 for LE scanning This sets the Filter_Duplicates parameter of LE Set Scan Enable command to LE_SCAN_FILTER_DUP_DISABLE (0x00). There is a conflict intention of receiving advertising reports in BlueZ where the Filter_Duplicates flag is set so the strict filtering with RSSI will be applied to Intel BT controllers. However BlueZ checks if HCI_QUIRK_STRICT_DUPLICATE_FILTER is set and restarts LE scan if the bit is set in order to obtain the advertising reports dropped due to the strict filtering. By setting the Filter_Duplicates, BlueZ can potentially receive more advertising reports. BUG=b:64731753 TEST=emerge-eve sys-kernel/chromeos-kernel-4_4 ./update_kernel.sh --remote <IP to DUT> Confirms that the number of advertising reports increases in HCI traffics. CQ-DEPEND=CL:677740 Change-Id: Ic79c2c224d291b45f299295761bd7c19c8e19df5 Signed-off-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/677741 Reviewed-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com>

FROMLIST: PM / mfd: intel-lpss: Push system sleep callbacks to late/early stages Push the system suspend/resume callbacks of intel-lpss to the late suspend/early resume stages to allow child device callbacks to be pushed to the late/early stages of suspend/resume too, so as to make it possible to avoid resuming the children if they are runtime- suspended during system suspend going forward. Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com> (am from ttps://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/9939809/) BUG=b:63121330 TEST=verify that no failures from camera suspend/resume time. Change-Id: I748b2398cb8d4ff717f9ab49496de0b015638a00 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/676272 Commit-Ready: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Tested-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hyungwoo Yang <hyungwoo.yang@intel.com>

FROMLIST/BACKPORT: PM / i2c: designware: Clean up system sleep handling After commit a23318feeff6 (i2c: designware: Fix system suspend) the i2c-designware-platdrv driver always resumes the device in its system sleep ->suspend callback which isn't particularly nice, even though it is technically correct. A better approach would be to make the driver track the PM state of the device so that it doesn't need to resume it in ->suspend, so implement it. First, drop dw_i2c_plat_suspend() added by commit a23318feeff6 and rename dw_i2c_plat_runtime_suspend() back to dw_i2c_plat_suspend(). Second, point the driver's ->late_suspend and ->early_resume callbacks, rather than its ->suspend and ->resume callbacks, to dw_i2c_plat_suspend() and dw_i2c_plat_resume(), respectively, so that they are not executed in parallel with each other, for example if runtime resume of the device takes place during system suspend. Finally, add "suspended" and "skip_resume" flags to struct dw_i2c_dev and make dw_i2c_plat_suspend() and dw_i2c_plat_resume() use them to avoid suspending or resuming the device twice in a row and to avoid resuming a previously runtime-suspended device during system resume. Overrides: a23318feeff6 (i2c: designware: Fix system suspend) Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com> (backported from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/9939807/) BUG=b:63121330 TEST=verify that no failures from camera suspend/resume time. paygen: Use the update_payload in update_engine Currently there are two version of the (almost) same code in platform/dev/host/lib/update_payload and aosp/system/update_engine/scripts We would like to use aops/system/update_engine/scripts instead for two reasons: 1) Not keeping duplicate code. 2) Prevent mistakes like forgetting to update dev/host/lib when new changes are landed in the update engine itself. This can cause the CQ to be fine but canary builds will fail. This patch changes all the update_payload references in chromite to src/aosp/system/update_engine/scripts/update_payload. Fizz: Control input current Fizz has an over current control system. There are two FETs connected to two registers: PR257 & PR258. These control thresholds of the over current control system. PR257, PR258 For 4.62A (90W BJ adapter), on, off For 3.33A (65W BJ adapter), off, on For 3.00A (Type-C adapter), off, off BJ adapters are distinguished by reading GPIO71. This patch also removes ISL9238 driver and ramping code. The charger chip has been removed from the board since proto2. BUG=b:65013352 BRANCH=none TEST=Boot Fizz Proto3 on BJ and Type-C. Change-Id: I32c2467f4ab23adf3f9313a03914d74d64a722df Signed-off-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/668119 Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org>
